### Complexometric Titration
A titration in which a soluble coordination complex is formed between a metal ion and a complexing agent (ligand) to determine the concentration of metal ions (such as water hardness).

### Reaction with EDTA:
EDTA (Ethylene Diamine Tetraacetic Acid, represented as $H_2Y^{2-}$ or $Na_2H_2Y$) reacts with metal ions ($M^{2+} = Ca^{2+}, Mg^{2+}$) to form stable, water-soluble metal-EDTA complexes:
$$\text{M}^{2+} + \text{H}_2\text{Y}^{2-} \rightarrow [\text{MY}]^{2-} + 2\text{H}^+$$
proTip: Remember that the buffer solution (usually $NH_4OH + NH_4Cl$) is maintained at $\text{pH} = 10$ during EDTA titrations to ensure stable complex formation.
